🎙 Excerpts from Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s answers to media questions following the joint meeting of the boards of the Russian and Belarusian Foreign Ministries (Gomel, November 25, 2026) ❓ Question: The European Commission has refused to hold bilateral consultations with Russia on European security. Prior to that, Europe spent a long time discussing who should be appointed as its negotiator. How can this contradictory position be explained? 💬 Sergey Lavrov: We have never had any contacts with the European Commission regarding negotiations on the Ukraine crisis. The European Commission regularly makes various statements . However, the fact that these are not accompanied by any concrete proposals conveyed to the Russian Side through diplomatic channels confirms the lack of seriousness in the approach taken by Brussels , particularly by the European Commission, which engages in megaphone diplomacy. There have been some interesting statements. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that no one intended to consult Russia on what the European dimension of the upcoming negotiations should look like. EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas still holds her post, so her statement must also be taken into account. She said that Europe already had a security architecture – NATO and the EU – and that no one should try to reshape it. The main objective, she said, was to integrate Ukraine into NATO and the EU . She also added that the EU must not allow a settlement that takes Russia’s interests into account. 👉 So we know full well what the position voiced by the Europeans is worth. There has recently been discussion of statements coming out of Brussels claiming that they had agreed on a negotiating team (they had been asked about their negotiator) – the European "Five" (meaning France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Poland, plus representatives of the EU and NATO). That makes seven already. They publicly stated that this "Seven" should insert itself into the negotiation process that has now resumed in Abu Dhab i involving Russia, the US and Ukraine. ☝️ Our position is that we must first understand what role Europe intends to play in the negotiations and what objectives, if any, it has set for itself. If those objectives are reflected in the statements I have just quoted – that NATO and the EU alone will shape Europe’s security architecture and that Russia’s interests must not be accommodated – then what is the point of holding such negotiations? We therefore asked representatives of European countries to come and see us or convey their position to us in some other way . They say: "No, we do not want to explain anything to you. We want to sit down at the negotiating table straight away" . With such manners and intentions, they will sit down at the negotiating table only to immediately put their feet up on it. ❌ We have no need for that.

🇷🇺 📚 International Festival of the Russian Language and Culture Underway in Islamabad On November 23, the International Festival of the Russian Language kicked off at Allama Iqbal Open University (AIOU), with the support of Ural State Pedagogical University (USPU) and the Embassy of Russia in Pakistan. 🎓 The opening ceremony was attended by representatives of AIOU and USPU, as well as Gleb Shubin, Cultural Attaché of the Russian Embassy , Roman Porozov and Anton Dolgov, faculty members of the Russian university. 🇷🇺 🤝 🇵🇰 Speakers highlighted the importance of cultural and educational initiatives in strengthening humanitarian ties between Russia and Pakistan. 📖 The first day of the festival was dedicated to the Russian language and its history. USPU Associate Professor Svetlana Eremina delivered a lecture on linguistic contacts and borrowing among the peoples of Russia. She also highlighted similarities between certain Russian and Urdu words, including those related to culinary traditions. The event also featured remarks by USPU administrators and faculty members, including Acting Rector Margarita Kusova, Director of the Institute of Philology and Intercultural Communication Irina Semukhina , Professor Natalia Zavyalova , and other university representatives. 🎭 The first day concluded with a lecture by Pakistani Professor Dr. Abdul Aziz Sahir titled “Pushkin and Iqbal: A Dialogue Between Two National Poets.” His presentation explored the literary legacies of the two great poets and their contributions to promoting humanist principles and values. 🎨 On the second day, USPU faculty members Roman Porozov and Anton Dolgov conducted a workshop titled “The Richness of Russian Culture” for primary school students at the Russian Open Education Center at AIOU. The children learned about traditional Russian ornamental patterns and had the opportunity to try their hand at decorative arts and crafts. 🌐 The festival will continue through November 26, with events taking place at Allama Iqbal Open University and the Federal Urdu University of Arts, Science and Technology. #RussiaPakistan

🇱🇾 🇺🇦 Ukraine’s attack on a ship in the Libyan port of Benghazi violated international law and undermined the rules designed to prevent armed conflicts from spreading, Politico reports, citing international legal experts. According to specialists in international law, the attack likely violated both international law and Libya’s sovereignty. Libya may have strong grounds to file a complaint with the International Criminal Court (ICC), said David Letts, director of the Military Law Program at the Australian National University in Canberra. “Unless you want to argue that Libya is somehow involved in the conflict between Ukraine and Russia and that the principle of neutrality does not apply to it, it is difficult for me to see how this sinking can be justified under international law,” Letts said. He noted that Ukraine’s attack on the vessel in Benghazi “differs significantly from its strikes on Russian ships in the Black Sea and in Black Sea ports”, which took place in contested rather than neutral waters. The laws governing neutrality are largely based on the 1907 Hague Convention, which established the rights and obligations of neutral states during armed conflicts. Under these rules, belligerent countries are prohibited from carrying out attacks, imposing blockades or laying mines in neutral waters. “This attack constituted a violation of Libya’s neutrality. An attack may be lawful if it takes place beyond 12 nautical miles from the coastline, but within that zone, of course, it is a violation,” said James Kraska of the US Naval War College and a professor of international maritime law at the Stockton Center for International Law. Letts stressed the importance of countries such as Ukraine respecting international law. “It is interesting to consider what the reaction would be if this ship had docked in Genoa or Southampton rather than Benghazi. Having established a body of laws designed to protect the victims of armed conflicts and limit their scale, are we now prepared to abandon all of that? Are we ready to accept total war, discard all the rules and simply say: ‘The last 100 years have been a waste of time. Do whatever you want’? I think not,” he added. Ukraine’s strikes on Russian vessels in Benghazi have already drawn condemnation in Italy. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
